runtimes.name: browser
runtimes.version: any (ES2015+ / modern Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
runtimes.source: index.html — uses vanilla JS with no transpilation; no package.json or .nvmrc found

runtimes.name: python3
runtimes.version: any (optional — only needed to serve via HTTP)

checklist.label: Open index.html directly in a modern browser
checklist.failurePoint: Some browsers restrict fetch() under the file:// protocol — use the HTTP server option if panels fail to load JSON

checklist.label: Click all five nav tabs (Overview, Architecture, Setup, Ask, First Task) and confirm each panel renders
checklist.failurePoint: If JS is disabled or file encoding is not UTF-8 the nav will be unresponsive — enable JS and ensure UTF-8 save

checklist.label: In the Ask tab, type how are expenses categorized? and confirm a response appears
checklist.failurePoint: No response means the sendChat() function is blocked — open browser DevTools console (F12) to see the error

checklist.label: Optional: serve via HTTP to enable full fetch() support: python3 -m http.server 8000 then open http://localhost:8000
checklist.failurePoint: Port 8000 already in use — change the port number: `python3 -m http.server 8080`

failurePoints.description: fetch() calls are blocked under the file:// protocol in some browsers (Chrome is strictest), so output/*.json files may not load.
failurePoints.fix: Use the optional HTTP server: `python3 -m http.server 8000` from the codesensei-scaffold/ directory, then open http://localhost:8000

failurePoints.description: Port 8000 already bound by another process.
failurePoints.fix: Try an alternate port: `python3 -m http.server 8080` or `python3 -m http.server 3000`

script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# CodeSensei — zero-dependency static HTML prototype
# No package manager, no build step, no environment variables required.

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

echo "CodeSensei setup"
echo "================"
echo "No dependencies to install."
echo ""

if command -v python3 &>/dev/null; then
  PORT=8000
  # Try fallback ports if 8000 is busy
  for p in 8000 8080 3000 4000; do
    if ! lsof -Pi ":$p" -sTCP:LISTEN -t &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
      PORT=$p
      break
    fi
  done
  echo "Starting HTTP server on port $PORT..."
  echo "Open: http://localhost:$PORT"
  python3 -m http.server "$PORT"
else
  echo "Python3 not found."
  echo "Open index.html directly in your browser, or install Python 3 for HTTP server support."
fi
